question.text: For a reaction taking place in a container in equilibrium with its surroundings, the effect of temperature on its equilibrium constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> in terms of change in entropy is described by:

options.text: with increase in temperature, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> for exothermic reaction decreases because the entropy change of the system is positive.

with increase in temperature, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> for endothermic reaction increases because unfavourable change in entropy of the surroundings decreases.

with increase in temperature, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> for exothermic reaction decreases because favourable change in entropy of the surroundings decreases.

with increase in temperature, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> for endothermic reaction increases because the entropy change of the system is negative.

solution.text:
ΔSsurrounding=-qprocessTsurrounding

If ΔH>0, on increasing temperature, Kequilibrium also increase, so ΔSsurrounding<0 (Surrounding is unfavourable).

If ΔH<0, on increasing temperature Kequilibrium, decreases, so ΔSsurrounding>0 (Surrounding is favourable).
